Done. `PLAYGROUND/submission.md` is written and the deliverable is in OUTPUT.

## What I found on arrival

The run had been interrupted at ~03:02 and the master re-entered round 1 with `--force`, leaving the playground intact — so an `answer.tex` already existed. `state.json` shows `rounds: 0` and there's no p2 validator report in `logs/`, so **the validator never ran and there was no feedback to respond to**. This is a first submission, not a revision. I treated the inherited draft as unverified and re-checked it from scratch.

## Verification

- **Source**: `diff` of the ingested text against `input/os_hw_3_problems.md` → identical; the brief's verbatim block matches line 5 word for word. No brief/source discrepancy. (R7's image and figure channels genuinely don't exist here — the manifest records the file as `kind: text_document`; this question refers to no figure.)
- **Every number**, re-derived in SI units in a throwaway script sharing no code with `calc_size_latency.py`: 168,000 mm², 409.88 mm side, 2.3767 wafers, 2.7344 ns round trip, 10.94 cycles @ 4 GHz. All match what the answer quotes.
- **Both external figures**, by web search: 0.021 µm² is the published TSMC N5 HD SRAM cell (and the densest production cell reported); ~32 Mib/mm² — the constant the area cross-check leans on — is that same source's derived density; L1/L2/L3 at ~4/14/40 cycles sits mid-range of published measurements.

## Two defects I fixed

My own audit turned up two real problems, both in load-bearing sentences:

1. The thesis claimed material and size "cannot be chosen independently" — muddy and arguably false, since they plainly can. The actual claim is that **size dominates** at terabyte scale.
2. "That time is bounded below by the array's linear dimension" bounded a *time* by a *length* — a dimensional category error sitting inside the physics argument, and the first thing a hostile reader would pick at.

Net 364 → 368 words, inside the 300–380 target. I rewrapped the source afterwards and confirmed via `pdftotext` diff that the rendered page is byte-identical, so the rewrap touched source only.

## State

`answer.tex` compiles rc=0, one page, zero Overfull/Underfull boxes, no warnings; I rendered and read the page. R5-clean (no `\documentclass`/`\usepackage`/document env), no labels or figures so nothing to namespace, no `preamble.txt` needed. `lint_output.py` exits 0 with `answer.tex` as the only file.

The weakest point, flagged for the validator: the 4/14/40 cycle counts are the one claim with no computation behind them — verified as typical by search, but a citation rather than a measurement. The argument only needs the three to differ by about an order of magnitude end to end, which isn't in dispute.

Sources: [WikiChip N5](https://en.wikichip.org/wiki/N5), [SemiWiki — TSMC 5nm 0.021µm² SRAM cell, ISSCC 2020](https://semiwiki.com/semiconductor-manufacturers/tsmc/283487-tsmcs-5nm-0-021um2-sram-cell-using-euv-and-high-mobility-channel-with-write-assist-at-isscc2020/), [UCI CS250B — Cache and Memory System](https://www.ics.uci.edu/~swjun/courses/2023F-CS250B/material/lec2%20-%20Cache%20And%20Memory%20System.pdf)
